want.who_she_is: Cass Ridley, 24. Eighteen months of it belonging to somebody else, four weeks served. A rented room over a laundry on the east side, a monitor on her left ankle, and a job at a hardware and pawn shop because the shop is one of two places in the zone that will sign an hours sheet. What she has to lose: the fourteen months she is not doing — a violation is custody, and the game says so in plain words on the first screen.
want.obligation: Delgado, Tuesdays at two, at the county office, with the sheet due Friday and her signature under his. And a second enforcer that is not a person: the box — a radius drawn around her room, home by eight, and a battery that holds eighteen hours.
want.collector_note: §4a — he holds the obligation and is NOT the pipe the porn comes down. Field collectors carry 0.4-3.8% of a game's explicit passages and are never the top figure. Delgado has ONE surface, at `vouch 60`, and arrives late. The lint `the collector is also the target` reads this.
want.appetite: To be in a room nobody can place her in, and to be wanted while she is in it. It cannot be finished for a structural reason rather than a poetic one: every room she gets into becomes a room she is known in. The box logs a point every sixty seconds, Marty knows her hours, Rae knows when she comes down the stairs, and Delgado has all of it on one page every Tuesday. The appetite renews out of its own successes. WHERE THE HOLD STOPS BEING THE REASON: the week the box comes off, nobody is owed anything by anyone, and at 19:45 she walks the same route to the same back room.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: six streets — her room, the laundry under it, Marty's shop, the county office, the lot behind the shop, the bus stop where the line runs. Home by eight, and every door she walks through is a row in a log somebody else reads on Tuesday. TOP: the far side of the river after midnight, in rooms that are not in any zone, with people who sign her sheet without reading it, and the box on the desk at home saying she is asleep.
want.charge: reversal (primary) + transformation (late, secondary) — every adult in her life holds a signature over her, and the ascent is her collecting those signatures one at a time; each one collected is a person who now has something to lose. The transformation is §2's last line stated as a moment.

why_this_person.npc_marty: 50s, owns the shop, wife works nights. The first person since the sentence who treats her as an employee instead of a case number — and she can feel exactly what it costs him to keep doing it. Being wanted by him is being wanted by the one man who has read the file and hires her anyway.
why_this_person.npc_tobin: 26, services the boxes out of the county office, bored out of his skull. He holds the only thing she actually wants and treats it as nothing. The cheapest transaction in the game, and she knows it while it is happening.
why_this_person.npc_rae: Runs the laundry, owns the building, up at four. The only person who has never once asked what Cass did — and therefore the only person whose good opinion Cass could still lose.
why_this_person.npc_delgado: The officer. Knows every true thing about her and is scrupulously correct about all of it, which is what makes any slip the loudest event in the game.

board_intent.note: NOT the board. These are the §3 declarations the Want fixed, carried forward so the board phase checks itself against them rather than re-deriving. the-systems.md is read FIRST in that phase.
board_intent.counterweight: clean — the fourteen months. A brake, never the dominant meter; the world does not contract as it falls, it only gets louder about the price. At zero: the hearing, a terminal state shipped on purpose.
board_intent.rung_note: RUNGS DELIBERATELY DO NOT START AT 15. All 16 declared tiers across five v2 games sit at exactly 15 because templates/board.toml shipped that table. Field runs 8-17 rungs starting near 5. radius 5/12/20/30/45/60/80 · hours 5/15/25/40/55/70/85 · vouch 5/15/30/45/60/80.
board_intent.map_archetype: nested_zones — chosen over map_hotspots, which the radius argues for: hotspots wants 10+ drawn districts and this game opens with six streets, so it would ship a map that is mostly locked pictures. board_intent.economy_note: hold_kind = order, so want.economy's obligation/obligation_amount/week_income are deliberately ABSENT and gate 24 reports n/a — which the-want.md §1b calls a choice, not an omission. Money still has to gate something (gate 16) and what it buys still has to open a door (R1b); that is the board phase's problem, not the hold's.
board_intent.release_41: Asked of `hours`: a night band on a room that already exists. The laundry at 02:00 is not the laundry. Eleven locations x the hours ladder is the content schedule, and it needs no new ground.
board_intent.battery_need: THE PREMISE AS A METER. The box holds 18 hours; the dock is 90 minutes and it is in her room. Under 20% she cannot leave the zone at all; under 5% the alarm goes to Delgado's desk. This is why 19:45 in somebody else's back room is a scene and not a decision. ⚠️ The trait was called `charge` until 2026-09-05; renamed because in a sidebar row beside food/rest/wash it read as HER battery. She is a human woman with a court order. The sidebar label is `The box`.

`charge` (renamed `battery` 2026-09-05) is the SPENT shape, not decay. Verified: player_trait_decay fires only inside advanceDay() (v2.py:5733/:5826), so an 18-hour battery cannot be a daily decay. It is priced with `costs` on every time-advancing choice outside her room, and the engine filters the choice when she cannot pay (v2.py:4902).

The wardrobe is `worn_type neq covers_ankle` — does the box show. One derived read the whole world tests, which is DoL's $exposed shape (~900 reads, 82% colour). Our repo reads worn_exposure 3 times across 26 games.
Money buys a DOCK, on a level ladder with COMPOUND gates (money AND trust, money AND vouch AND ankle). R1b: money alone never buys the next tier in the field, and what it buys is read forever after.

Opening is a STAGED open with cast load ONE — Delgado enters, is described, speaks, states what he wants, and nobody else is named. F1 is a consistency rule (cast load vs word budget), not a word count; our measured failure named six people, two not in the game.

Delgado's Thursday summons is a CANVAS gated on `clean < 40`, not a conditional schedule row. His 14:00-16:00 Thu row always exists. Nothing in this design assumes the engine can gate a schedule.

Tobin's late diner window is authored as TWO rows ([4,5] 23:00-23:59 and [5,6] 00:00-01:00) because a day-specific overnight window deletes the character at midnight (v2.py:3596-3597). Rae's 22:00-04:00 is ONE row because it covers all seven weekdays.

Naming drift caught by LO 2026-09-05: the economy's sources line said shifts were 'energy-priced' while the declared need key is `rest`. There is no `energy` meter in this game. Renamed the prose; the key was always `rest`. `charge` (renamed `battery` 2026-09-05) is the ankle monitor's battery and is a SEPARATE meter from her tiredness — the two pull in opposite directions on purpose, and both are refilled in the same room.

LO read the sidebar as a player and asked whether the lead is a humanoid. The trait `charge` is RENAMED `battery`. Cause named: the only other game in this repo with a `Charge up` / `Power down` body is vesper, whose lead IS company-owned property (the-meters.md M8), and that vocabulary was carried into a game about a human on a court order. Worse than a stray word because of placement — in a sidebar row beside food/rest/wash, a fourth bar reads as her body. Sidebar now renders it as `The box` with word bands, so it names the DEVICE. 25 sites across 6 files; free today, frozen after 0.1 because a trait key is a save join-key. `want.charge` is UNTOUCHED — that is the dramatic charge (reversal/taboo/transformation), a different word.
